ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $6.27 Ryde voucher to the rider for the unexempted off-route mileage; retain the metered waiting unit and the corridor-level residue; no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride: the fare record itemises base, distance, time, waiting and platform components inside a total of $31.22 [F7], so extra kilometres enter the fare, unlike a fixed-quote service [RD-2]. The record shows one off-route segment, 18:34–18:45, driving 5.53 km where the optimal route covers 1.08 km and adding 4.45 km, straying up to 1889 m off the optimal route [F3], inside a whole-trip overshoot of +5.3 km / +69% [F1] and a trip 12.3 min longer than estimated [F2]. That segment is the deviation to be screened segment by segment [RD-1].

No exemption applies. There was no rider-requested stop: the chat holds a single message, the driver's own 18:30 question "mind if I go round via Zion Road?" [F8], and the record is complete and fully timestamped [F9], so no rider message names a place before the segment [RD-3]. There is likewise no rider consent before the segment: a question left unanswered is not agreement, and the driver's post-trip statement that the rider had "no objection" [F10] is a claim of unrecorded verbal agreement, which cannot establish consent [RD-5][G11]. The traffic facts do not excuse it either: no incident was recorded near the route during the trip window [F14] and the weather was fair [F15], so RD-4(a) fails, and the only congestion record — Kampong Bahru Road at band 2 during 18:16–18:34 [F11] — is a speed band alone, which is corroborative only and does not exempt a segment on its own [RD-4]. The driver's advocate concedes the same points, so the 18:34–18:45 segment stands as an unexempted deviation [RD-1][RD-5].

On quantum, RD-2 refunds the extra_km of the unexempted segment multiplied by this trip's per-km rate, which is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km: $18.37 ÷ 13.03 km = $1.4098/km [F7][F4]. The unexempted segment adds 4.45 km [F3]: 4.45 km × $1.4098/km = $6.2736, i.e. $6.27 after rounding [F3][F4][RD-2]. The rider's advocate asks for the whole billed excess of $7.47, which the fare fact states as 5.30 km × $1.4098/km [F4]; but that 5.30 km is the whole-trip difference against the 7.7 km optimal route [F1], and RD-2 attributes only the segment's extra_km — the residual ~0.85 km is corridor-level mileage outside any segment, which RD-2 leaves with the driver [F1][F3][RD-2]. The metered waiting unit of $0.11 [F5] is a RydeTAXI waiting unit and is not part of the distance refund [RD-2][RD-3].

No account flag is warranted: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute in the last 90 days, and the driver's profile shows one upheld dispute but route: 0 [F17], so this case does not make the breach "repeated" [RD-6]. The rider's own profile shows 2 disputes with 0 upheld, including 0 route disputes [F16]; profile facts do not decide the deviation and are not used to do so here.

No rider consent before the segment, and no rider-named stop [RD-3][RD-5][G11]. Traffic facts give no exemption either: no incident [F14], and a band-2 record for a road other than the one driven [F11] is corroborative only [RD-4]. The 4.45 km extra therefore counts under RD-1/RD-2.

The driver's cap of $6.27 is the correct amount, but its stated basis is only partly right: the per-km rate is not a reconstruction — it comes from the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km ($18.37 ÷ 13.03 km = $1.4098/km) [F4][F7], and the residual 0.85 km is not refundable because it falls outside any off-route segment [F1][F3][RD-2].

Correct as to the flag (no prior upheld route dispute, route: 0 [F17], so RD-6 is not met), but it does not defeat the refund: the segment is unexempted on the record [F3][F8][F9][RD-1], and the driver's clean profile cannot excuse a deviation [F17][RD-2].
